title: Adapting LLM-SC to Living Sacred Heritage: Domain-Specific Extraction, Semantic Networks and Human Evaluation on Pashupatinath Temple Reviews
abstract: arXiv:2610.35685v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) pipelines can turn visitor reviews into structured data, but generic schemes may miss rituals, sacred spaces, cultural restrictions and emotionally mixed experiences at living sacred heritage sites. We adapted the LLM-Social Computing (LLM-SC) framework to Pashupatinath Temple, Nepal, by specifying a 12-type entity taxonomy (four original LLM-SC types plus eight sacred-heritage types), four relation types and nine aspect-sentiment dimensions in a GPT-4o extraction prompt, which was applied to a fixed random sample of 2,500 English-language Tripadvisor reviews from a processed corpus of 3,939. The exports contain 11,286 entity, 6,232 aspect-sentiment and 5,590 relation records, covering 2,485, 2,487 and 2,433 reviews, respectively; the eight added sacred-heritage types account for 64.8% of entity records. Against an adjudicated two-annotator reference for 200 reviews, exact normalized surface-and-type matching

translated_title: 将LLM-SC框架适配于活态神圣遗产：基于帕斯帕提那神庙游客评论的领域特定信息提取、语义网络与人工评估
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）流水线可以将游客评论转化为结构化数据，但通用方案可能会遗漏活态神圣遗产场所中的宗教仪式、神圣空间、文化限制以及情感复杂的体验。我们通过在GPT-4o提取提示词中明确指定一个包含12种类型的实体分类体系（4种原始LLM-SC类型加8种神圣遗产类型）、4种关系类型和9个方面-情感维度，将LLM-社会计算（LLM-SC）框架适配到尼泊尔帕斯帕提那神庙，并将其应用于从3,939条处理后语料中固定随机抽取的2,500条英文Tripadvisor评论。导出的数据包含11,286条实体记录、6,232条方面-情感记录和5,590条关系记录，分别覆盖2,485、2,487和2,433条评论；其中新增的8种神圣遗产类型占实体记录的64.8%。以200条评论的双标注者仲裁参考标准为基准，精确的规范化表层与类型匹配……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究将LLM-SC框架适配到尼泊尔帕斯帕提那神庙这一活态神圣遗产场景，通过新增8种神圣遗产实体类型构建12类实体分类体系，从Tripadvisor评论中成功提取结构化数据，且新增的神圣遗产类型占实体记录的64.8%，证明领域特定适配对宗教遗产评论分析至关重要。
en_tdlr: This study adapts the LLM-SC framework to living sacred heritage at Nepal's Pashupatinath Temple by extending the entity taxonomy with eight sacred-heritage types (12 in total), successfully extracting structured data from Tripadvisor reviews, and demonstrating that the added sacred-heritage types account for 64.8% of entity records.
